rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says malāʾika is the plural of malak; the singular without hamza is more common in Arabic, with the hamza dropped and the formerly still lām vowelled.
rows.anchor: فسميت الملائكة ملائكة بالرسالة، لأنها رسل الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He connects the name malāʾika to risāla, since angels carry God’s messages between Him and prophets and servants to whom they are sent; the cited line uses aliknī for delivering a message.
rows.anchor: ألكني إليها عمرك الله يا فتى … بآية ما جاءت إلينا تهاديا يعني بذلك: أبلغها رسالتي

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada understand إني جاعل as I am doing or making, rather than specifically creating.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن، وأبي بكر يعني الهذلي، عن الحسن، وقتادة، قالوا

rows.speaker: أبو روق
rows.claim: Abu Rawq reports a general rule that every occurrence of jaʿala in the Qur’an means created.
rows.anchor: عن أبي روق، قال: «كل شيء في القرآن جعل فهو خلق»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers that God will install a successor in the earth and make a replacement there, which he says best accords with Hasan and Qatada’s interpretation.
rows.anchor: والصواب في تأويل قوله: {إني جاعل في الأرض خليفة} [البقرة: 30] أي مستخلف في الأرض

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says the earth was spread from Mecca, angels first circumambulated the House, and it was the earth meant here; surviving prophets and their followers later worshipped there, with several prophets’ graves between Zamzam and the Black Stone and Station.
rows.anchor: عن ابن سابط، أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī derives khalīfa as a faʿīla form from someone succeeding another in an affair and taking his place after him.
rows.anchor: قولك: خلف فلان فلانا في هذا الأمر إذا قام مقامه فيه بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He links the sense to 10:14: God made a later people successors in the earth after their predecessors, replacing them.
rows.anchor: ثم جعلناكم خلائف في الأرض من بعدهم لننظر كيف تعملون} [يونس: 14] يعني بذلك: أنه أبدلكم في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The supreme ruler is called khalīfa because he succeeds the previous ruler and takes his place in governing.
rows.anchor: ومن ذلك قيل للسلطان الأعظم: خليفة، لأنه خلف الذي كان قبله، فقام بالأمر مقامه

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq takes khalīfa to mean an inhabitant and cultivator unlike the angels; al-Ṭabarī rejects this as the meaning, despite God saying the figure would inhabit the earth.
rows.anchor: وليس الذي قال ابن إسحاق في معنى الخليفة بتأويلها، وإن كان الله جل ثناؤه إنما أخبر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that jinn first inhabited earth and shed blood; God sent Iblis with angels to defeat and expel them, then placed Adam there as their successor.
rows.anchor: عن الضحاك، عن ابن عباس، قال

rows.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
rows.claim: Al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas says angels were created Wednesday, jinn Thursday, and Adam Friday; when some jinn disbelieved, angels fought them, producing bloodshed and corruption on earth.
rows.anchor: حدثنا إسحاق، قال: حدثنا عبد الله بن أبي جعفر، عن أبيه، عن الربيع بن أنس

rows.speaker: الحسن البصري
rows.claim: Al-Hasan al-Basri is credited with reading khalīfa as successive generations: Adam’s descendants replace their father and each generation succeeds the one before it.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول حكي عن الحسن البصري

rows.speaker: ابن سابط
rows.claim: Ibn Sābit says the angels’ description of those who corrupt and shed blood refers to Adam’s children.
rows.anchor: عن عطاء بن السائب، عن ابن سابط: في قوله

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd reports that God planned to create a creature and make a khalīfa in an earth then without creatures, apart from the angels.
rows.anchor: حدثني يونس، قال: أخبرنا ابن وهب، قال: قال ابن زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says Ibn Zayd’s statement could mean generational succession, as in Hasan’s view, or that God would appoint a khalīfa to judge among creatures by His judgment.
rows.anchor: وهذا القول يحتمل ما حكي عن الحسن، ويحتمل أن يكون أراد ابن زيد أن الله أخبر الملائكة

rows.speaker: السدي، عن ابن عباس وابن مسعود وأصحاب النبي
rows.claim: In a report through al-Suddi from Ibn Abbas, Ibn Masud and Companions, God says the khalīfa will have descendants who corrupt, envy one another and kill one another.
rows.anchor: عن أبي مالك، وعن أبي صالح، عن ابن عباس، وعن مرة، عن ابن مسعود، وعن ناس، من أصحاب النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this report’s reading, the khalīfa is Adam and those who succeed him in obeying God and judging His creatures justly; corruption and unjust bloodshed belong to their descendants, not these deputies.
rows.anchor: فكان تأويل الآية على هذه الرواية التي ذكرناها عن ابن مسعود وابن عباس: إني جاعل في الأرض خليفة مني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This reading agrees with Hasan’s view in separating the khalīfa from the corrupt, but differs because it makes Adam God’s appointed deputy while Hasan means generations succeeding one another and assigns corruption to the khalīfa.
rows.anchor: وهذا التأويل وإن كان مخالفا في معنى الخليفة ما حكي عن الحسن من وجه، فموافق له من وجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī rejects the inference that the angels explicitly blamed God’s khalīfa: they said only one would corrupt, so God could have told them the khalīfa’s descendants would do so, as the Ibn Masud and Ibn Abbas report says.
rows.anchor: بل قالت: {أتجعل فيها من يفسد فيها} [البقرة: 30] وغير منكر أن يكون ربها أعلمها أنه يكون لخليفته ذلك ذرية

words: أَتَجْعَلُ فِيهَا مَن يُفْسِدُ فِيهَا وَيَسْفِكُ ٱلدِّمَآءَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī asks how angels could know before Adam and his descendants existed that the khalīfa’s people would corrupt and shed blood: did they know the unseen, or merely conjecture and speak without knowledge?
rows.anchor: أعلمت الغيب فقالت ذلك، أم قالت ما قالت من ذلك ظنا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas’s account says Iblis was a fire-born angelic being called al-Hinn, named al-Harith and a keeper of Paradise; jinn first corrupted earth, and Iblis’s angelic force defeated them, prompting the angels’ question, while God knew Iblis’s hidden pride.
rows.anchor: عن الضحاك، عن ابن عباس، قال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The same account says God had Adam’s soil raised and formed him from sticky clay; his body lay for forty nights, and Iblis struck it, entered and exited it, before the spirit entered through Adam’s head.
rows.anchor: عن الضحاك، عن ابن عباس، قال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In Ibn Abbas’s report, Adam’s haste is linked to human impatience; he praises God at a sneeze, Iblis refuses prostration from pride and is expelled, then Adam names things, while the angels disclaim unseen knowledge and God exposes Iblis’s concealed pride.
rows.anchor: وهذه الرواية عن ابن عباس تنبئ عن أن قول الله جل ثناؤه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī reads the address as directed to a particular angelic faction, Iblis’s companions who fought the jinn, to test them, expose their limited knowledge, and show that honor comes without bodily strength.
rows.anchor: وأن الذين قيل لهم ذلك من الملائكة كانوا قبيلة إبليس خاصة، الذين قاتلوا معه جن الأرض قبل خلق آدم

words: أَتَجْعَلُ فِيهَا مَن يُفْسِدُ فِيهَا وَيَسْفِكُ ٱلدِّمَآءَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He calls the angels’ question a lapse and conjecture about the unseen; they were shown their error, repented and disclaimed unseen knowledge, while God exposed Iblis’s hidden arrogance.
rows.anchor: ويصرح بأن قيلهم لربهم: {أتجعل فيها من يفسد فيها ويسفك الدماء} [البقرة: 30] كانت هفوة منهم ورجما بالغيب

rows.speaker: السدي عن أبي مالك وأبي صالح وابن عباس وابن مسعود وأصحاب النبي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi’s report from Ibn Abbas, Ibn Masud and Companions says Iblis ruled a heaven, grew proud, and angels were told the khalīfa’s descendants would corrupt, envy and kill; their question followed. The account then tells how angels collected multicolored clay despite earth’s pleas, explaining human diversity, and Adam was formed from it.
rows.anchor: عن السدي، في خبر ذكره عن أبي مالك، وعن أبي صالح، عن ابن عباس، وعن مرة، عن ابن مسعود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī continues the al-Suddi account: Iblis calls Adam hollow and vows to destroy him; when the spirit reaches Adam, he sees fruit, hungers and rushes toward it before the spirit reaches his feet, illustrating human haste.
rows.anchor: فقال للملائكة: لا ترهبوا من هذا، فإن ربكم صمد وهذا أجوف، لئن سلطت عليه لأهلكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account continues: angels prostrate except proud Iblis, who is expelled; Adam names the creatures, the angels acknowledge they know only what God taught, and God reveals the pride Iblis concealed.
rows.anchor: فسجد الملائكة كلهم أجمعون إلا إبليس أبى أن يكون مع الساجدين أي استكبر وكان من الكافرين

words: أَتَجْعَلُ فِيهَا مَن يُفْسِدُ فِيهَا وَيَسْفِكُ ٱلدِّمَآءَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says this report’s opening differs from the earlier Ibn Abbas account, while its ending agrees in the angels’ admission of ignorance and disclosure of Iblis’s pride.
rows.anchor: فهذا الخبر أوله مخالف معناه معنى الرواية التي رويت عن ابن عباس من رواية الضحاك

words: أَتَجْعَلُ فِيهَا مَن يُفْسِدُ فِيهَا وَيَسْفِكُ ٱلدِّمَآءَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī argues that if God had already told angels the descendants would corrupt and shed blood, they could not be reproached for repeating that fact or challenged to name what God had hidden.
rows.anchor: وهذا إذا تدبره ذو الفهم، علم أن أوله يفسد آخره، وأن آخره يبطل معنى أوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He suspects a transmitter misreported the account; a plausible original reading is that angels inferred too much from God’s statement about corrupt descendants and were challenged to prove what they presumed to know.
rows.anchor: وأخشى أن يكون بعض نقلة هذا الخبر هو الذي غلط على من رواه عنه من الصحابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this reconstruction, angels generalized from some descendants’ corruption to all of them; God had concealed that many would obey, reform the earth, preserve blood and attain honor.
rows.anchor: من طاعتهم ربهم وإصلاحهم في أرضه وحقن الدماء ورفعه منزلتهم وكرامتهم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī explicitly says this is his description of how the report may be interpreted, not the interpretation he chooses for the verse itself.
rows.anchor: وهذا الذي ذكرناه هو صفة منا لتأويل الخبر لا القول الذي نختاره في تأويل الآية
